title: To amend the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to authorize certain assessments by the Director of the Institute and impose requirements on certain memorandums of understanding relating to artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The amendment expands the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s authority to conduct assessments related to artificial intelligence and establishes specific requirements for memorandums of understanding that involve AI projects. It also includes additional provisions that are not detailed in the title.

title: To direct the Secretary of Commerce to support the adoption and use of American open artificial intelligence models, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Commerce to encourage the adoption and use of American-made, open‑source artificial intelligence models. It also sets out additional, unspecified measures to support AI development and deployment in the United States.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is designed to shield households from the rising electricity bills driven by AI data center operations. It proposes measures such as caps on energy use, subsidies, or tax incentives to keep AI‑related energy costs affordable for families.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes to pause the building and operation of new AI‑focused data centers until specific safety, regulatory, and environmental standards are established. This temporary halt is intended to give lawmakers and industry stakeholders time to assess the broader impacts of large‑scale AI infrastructure before it expands further.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law that seeks to make artificial intelligence systems more transparent and accountable by requiring companies to clearly disclose how AI works and what data it uses. It also sets guidelines for responsible AI development, including impact assessments, safety standards, and oversight to protect users and the public.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes mandatory safety, privacy, and content standards for AI‑enabled toys sold to children, requiring manufacturers to conduct rigorous testing and provide clear labeling. It also imposes data protection rules and age‑appropriate content guidelines to protect kids from harmful or inappropriate AI interactions.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is a law that protects children’s personal information when it is collected or used by artificial intelligence systems. It requires companies to obtain parental consent and provide clear, child-friendly privacy notices before gathering or processing any data from minors.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires a comprehensive report on how artificial intelligence is developed, used, and regulated within China. It mandates regular disclosures by AI firms and government bodies to promote transparency and help guide national AI policy.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a new law that requires companies developing or deploying artificial intelligence to report their AI systems’ energy consumption and power usage to regulators. The act aims to promote energy efficiency, reduce carbon footprints, and ensure transparency about the environmental impact of AI technologies.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act establishes rules for creating and using artificial intelligence models, aiming to keep users safe and protect privacy. It sets standards for transparency, accountability, and ethical use of AI technology.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This bill requires that every artificial‑intelligence system be accompanied by a detailed functional bill of materials that lists all software components, data sources, and hardware elements used in its development and deployment. It also includes additional provisions to promote transparency, safety, and regulatory compliance for AI technologies.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act aims to build a skilled workforce that can create, evaluate, and manage AI systems that people can trust. It proposes training programs, research funding, and partnerships between industry, academia, and government to ensure AI is safe, ethical, and reliable.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to reduce the environmental footprint of AI systems by requiring developers to measure and report energy use, carbon emissions, and resource consumption throughout a model’s lifecycle. It also establishes penalties for non‑compliance and mandates investment in green infrastructure to offset AI’s ecological impact.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to prevent AI companies from charging excessively high prices for their services and from manipulating wages in the labor market. It aims to protect consumers and workers by enforcing fair pricing and wage practices within the AI industry.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for using artificial intelligence in agriculture, ensuring that AI tools deployed in farming operations prioritize safety, transparency, and equitable access. It also requires data protection measures, oversight of AI-driven decision-making, and promotes research into sustainable AI practices for crop management.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: This act aims to encourage and streamline the use of artificial intelligence technologies in the financial services sector. It establishes supportive regulations and incentives to foster innovation while maintaining consumer protection and system stability.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act is a legislative effort to encourage the use of artificial intelligence across banks, fintech companies, and other financial institutions by easing regulatory hurdles and providing a clear framework for AI deployment. It aims to balance rapid technological progress with safeguards that protect consumer data, ensure financial stability, and promote responsible AI practices in the industry.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act aims to cultivate and retain AI expertise by offering incentives, funding, and educational programs that support the growth of a skilled workforce. It also promotes partnerships between government, academia, and industry to accelerate AI innovation while encouraging diversity and addressing ethical concerns.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act bars the creation of artificial‑intelligence data centers on property owned by the federal government, protecting those lands from high‑power, high‑heat facilities. The law requires any AI‑related computing infrastructure to be located elsewhere, ensuring federal lands remain free from the environmental and security impacts of large data centers.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to incorporate AI education into school curricula, ensuring that students gain foundational knowledge and skills related to artificial intelligence. It also seeks to prepare schools and educators for the responsible integration of AI tools in teaching, learning, and assessment practices.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a U.S. legislative proposal aimed at boosting students' understanding and preparedness for artificial intelligence. It seeks to integrate AI education into school curricula, provide teacher training, and establish resources for schools to adopt AI tools responsibly.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed regulation aimed at governing how artificial intelligence technologies are developed, deployed, and used. It seeks to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values while encouraging innovation and protecting users’ rights.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act aims to clarify how artificial intelligence can be integrated into educational settings. It outlines guidelines for teachers, students, and administrators to responsibly use AI tools while ensuring transparency and accountability.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says that every American and community affected by the construction or operation of an artificial‑intelligence data center has a right to full transparency about the project’s details. It also affirms that those communities should keep local autonomy, meaning they can influence decisions and control how the data center impacts them.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 establishes regulations for AI systems used in veteran care and benefits programs, requiring companies to demonstrate safety and fairness in their technology. It also creates oversight and accountability mechanisms to protect veterans from misuse or harm by AI.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: This act aims to protect people from deceptive or harmful AI-generated content that could lead to exploitation. It sets standards for transparency, accountability, and safeguards against fabricated information used to manipulate or harm vulnerable populations.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes guidelines and oversight mechanisms to ensure the safe, transparent, and accountable use of artificial intelligence in the judicial system. It also promotes research into AI’s impact on court processes and sets up frameworks for training, auditing, and ongoing evaluation.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This bill would mandate that a report be filed on how artificial intelligence is used when accessing unminimized information collected under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It also includes additional provisions related to AI oversight and other unspecified purposes.
